title: Laughter seized all his strong wellknit trunk.
html_source:
Kenner (Kenner, H. Joyce’s Voices, p71) describes the emergence of two narrative voices in Ulysses. One ‘is moving characters about and reporting their doings,in fluent unemphatic novelese, barely to be distinguished from a neutral idiom save by occasional “great searching eyes,” and occasional “strong wellknit trunk”……. . And while the first voice attends to the chapter’s housekeeping, a second narrative voice is uttering passages like the following

Woodshadows floated silently by through the morning peace from the stairhead seaward where he gazed. Inshore and farther out the mirror of water whitened, spurned by lightshod hurrying feet. White breast of the dim sea. The twining stresses, two by two. A hand plucking the harpstrings, merging their twining chords. Wavewhite wedded words shimmering on the dim tide.

They are written as Stephen is alone on the parapet in Telemachus. This second narrator does not explicitly indicate the words are those of Stephen’s, ‘but the sentences that brush them in absorb Stephen-words and Stephen-rhythms, moving us imperceptibly into Stephen’s thoughts’.
